en: Self-confidence and calm, especially in a difficult situation
hook: APLOMB: straight as a PLUMB line, perfectly steady.
story: When the stage lights failed mid-performance, the young singer handled it with aplomb, continuing in the dark and inviting the audience to light their phones. Aplomb means calm self-assurance under pressure. Synonyms: poise, composure.

en: Apt; very appropriate to the situation
hook: APPOSITE: APPROPRIATE and POSITioned just right.
story: In her farewell speech, the principal quoted an apposite line: 'Education is not filling a bucket, but lighting a fire.' It fit the moment perfectly. Apposite means highly appropriate. Don't confuse it with opposite. Synonyms: apt, pertinent, apropos.

en: Owing thanks or a duty to someone in return for help
hook: BEHOLDEN: HOLDEN (held) by a debt of gratitude.
story: The independent journalist refused donations from politicians because she didn't want to be beholden to anyone. To be beholden means to owe something to someone. Synonyms: indebted, obligated.

en: To make someone or something seem unimportant
hook: BE-LITTLE: make it LITTLE.
story: When Nadia shared her small business idea, her cousin belittled it: 'Selling cakes online? That's not a real business.' Two years later, she had twenty employees. To belittle is to make something seem unimportant. Synonyms: disparage, deprecate.

en: A group of similar things close together; to gather in a group
hook: CLUSTER: like a bunch of grapes clustered together.
story: A cluster of small shops grew around the new university gate: photocopy stores, tea stalls, and cheap cafés. Students clustered around the notice board to see results. A cluster is a group; to cluster is to gather closely.

en: Logical and consistent; clear and easy to understand
hook: CO-HERENT: all parts ADHERE together.
story: After the accident, the driver was too shocked to give a coherent account; his words came out jumbled. Later, calm again, he explained everything clearly. Coherent means logically connected and clear. Its opposite is incoherent.

en: To think deeply about; to consider as a possibility
hook: CONTEMPLATE: sit in the TEMPLE and think.
story: Sitting by the sea at Cox's Bazar, Arif contemplated his future. He was even contemplating quitting his job to start a business. To contemplate is to think deeply, or to consider doing something. Synonyms: ponder, ruminate.

en: Clever at achieving goals through deceit
hook: CRAFTY: CRAFTS clever tricks.
story: The crafty fox pretended to be injured to lure the chickens out of the coop. The crafty businessman used loopholes to avoid every tax. Crafty means cunning and sly. Synonyms: wily, artful, cunning.

en: To take apart; to gradually end a system
hook: DIS-MANTLE: remove the MANTLE (covering) piece by piece.
story: The workers dismantled the old stage after the concert, taking it apart piece by piece. Reformers vowed to dismantle the corrupt system. To dismantle is to take apart, physically or figuratively.

en: Detailed and complicated (adj.); to explain in more detail (verb)
hook: E-LABOR-ATE: lots of LABOR went into it.
story: Grandma prepared an elaborate feast: twelve dishes, each with its own complex recipe. When the teacher said, 'Can you elaborate?' she wanted more detail. Elaborate means detailed and complex, or to expand on something.

en: A critical explanation or interpretation of a text, especially scripture
hook: EXEGESIS: EXPLAINS the text, leading OUT (ex) its meaning.
story: The scholar spent forty years writing an exegesis of the ancient poem, explaining every line's meaning, history, and hidden references. Exegesis is detailed interpretation of a text, especially religious scripture.

en: To do without something pleasant; to give up
hook: FOR-GO: let it GO.
story: To save money for her GRE fee, Mitu forwent new clothes for Eid and skipped her friends' restaurant outings for three months. To forgo is to give up something desirable. Synonyms: relinquish, renounce.

en: Impossible to pass through; impossible to understand
hook: IM-PENETRABLE: can't PENETRATE it.
story: The forest was so thick it seemed impenetrable; not even sunlight reached the ground. The legal contract was equally impenetrable, full of jargon nobody could understand. Impenetrable means impossible to enter or understand.

en: Not allowing fluid to pass through; unaffected by
hook: IMPERVIOUS: nothing gets through, waterproof to water or criticism.
story: The new raincoat was impervious to water; Rafi stayed dry in the heaviest storm. His uncle was impervious to criticism too; no argument could change his mind. Impervious means not allowing entry, or not affected by.

en: Unable to be taken away or given away
hook: IN-ALIEN-ABLE: can't be made ALIEN (separated) from you.
story: The constitution declares that every citizen has inalienable rights: life, liberty, and the freedom to speak. No government can take them away. Inalienable means unable to be removed or transferred.

en: Having no skill; clumsy
hook: IN-EPT: NOT adept.
story: The inept new waiter spilled soup on three customers, mixed up every order, and dropped a tray of glasses, all in one hour. Inept means lacking skill. Its opposite is adept. Synonyms: incompetent, clumsy.

en: A strict disciplinarian who demands complete obedience
hook: MARTINET: named after Colonel MARTINET, a famously strict French drill master.
story: The new headmaster was a martinet: uniforms inspected daily, a fine for every minute of lateness, and silence in the corridors at all times. A martinet demands strict obedience to rules. Synonyms: taskmaster, disciplinarian.

en: A person excessively interested in themselves and their appearance
hook: NARCISSUS: fell in love with his own reflection.
story: The narcissist posted thirty selfies a day and turned every conversation back to himself: 'Enough about you, let's talk about me.' In Greek myth, Narcissus fell in love with his own reflection. A narcissist is excessively self-absorbed.

en: A harsh rebuke or scolding
hook: OBJURGATION: OBJECTION + a JURY's harsh verdict.
story: The coach's objurgation after the defeat lasted twenty minutes; no player dared look up. Objurgation means harsh scolding. Synonyms: rebuke, castigation, reprimand.

en: Just good enough; adequate
hook: PASSABLE: good enough to PASS, but no more.
story: Tanvir's cooking was passable: edible, not burnt, but nothing anyone would ask for twice. After the flood, the road was barely passable. Passable means adequate, or able to be traveled on.

en: Showing deep, sharp insight; piercing
hook: PENETRATING: goes straight through to the truth.
story: The interviewer asked a penetrating question that exposed the gap in the politician's plan. Her penetrating gaze made liars nervous. Penetrating means sharply insightful, or piercing. Synonyms: incisive, perceptive.

en: Visually charming, like a picture
hook: PICTURESQUE: PICTURE-perfect.
story: The picturesque village in Sylhet had tea gardens, winding paths, and mist on the hills every morning. Visitors photographed every corner. Picturesque means pretty in a quaint way, worth painting.

en: To think deeply or carefully; to show or reveal
hook: REFLECT: like a mirror, turning thoughts back on yourself.
story: On her birthday, Nadia reflected on the past year: what she learned, what she lost, and what she wanted next. Her calm voice reflected years of experience. To reflect is to think carefully, or to show something.

en: Able to find quick, clever ways to overcome difficulties
hook: RESOURCEFUL: full of RESOURCES in your mind.
story: When the power went out before the exam, resourceful Rafi studied by the light of his phone, then a candle, then the streetlight outside. Resourceful means good at finding solutions. Synonyms: ingenious, inventive.

en: To reduce costs or spending
hook: RE-TRENCH: dig back into a TRENCH, cutting back.
story: When sales collapsed, the company retrenched: it closed two branches, cut bonuses, and stopped hiring. To retrench is to cut back spending. In some countries, being retrenched means being laid off.

en: Excessively indulging one's own desires
hook: SELF-INDULGENT: INDULGING the SELF too much.
story: The director's three-hour film was self-indulgent: long scenes of himself thinking, staring at the sea, and reciting his own poetry. Self-indulgent means giving in to your own wishes too much. Synonyms: hedonistic, decadent.

en: To form a theory without firm evidence; to invest riskily
hook: SPECULATE: look (specere) ahead and guess.
story: Fans speculated wildly about why the star player was dropped: injury? A fight? Retirement? Nobody knew. Some people speculate on land, hoping prices will rise. To speculate is to guess without evidence, or to make risky investments.

en: Serious, respectable, and unadventurous
hook: STAID: STAYED the same forever, never adventurous.
story: The staid old bank had the same brown furniture, the same rules, and the same manager for forty years. Then a young CEO arrived with bright colors and mobile apps. Staid means sedate and unadventurous.

en: To forcibly stop; to prevent from being expressed
hook: SUP-PRESS: PRESS it down.
story: Mitu suppressed a laugh when the professor's glasses fell into his tea. The dictator suppressed the protests with force. To suppress is to hold back or put down. Synonyms: stifle, quash, subdue.

en: Remaining as a small trace of something that once was larger or more important
hook: VESTIGIAL: a VESTIGE, a remnant.
story: The human appendix is often called vestigial: a small leftover of an organ our ancestors used for digesting plants. A few vestigial customs from colonial times remain in court, like wigs. Vestigial means remaining as a trace.
